brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.requirement: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching
requirements.evidence: Current build has drawer: drawer:0#0,0#cut on half-n base at 0,0,0. Spike at same corner is not offered by configurator – find_sockets for spike returns 0 with half base present, and with full bases at 0,0,0 0,1,0 1,0,0 the only spike junction is 0,0|0,1|1,0 which is the opposite corner from a notch drawer at 1,1. Placing both at identical junction is refused by configurator rules (SPIKE_CLASH / no socket) – meshes would intersect. No alternative socket achieves touching co-location.

finish.summary: Built half-base with drawer to show closest possible drawer; configurator offers no spike at the same corner of that cell, and with full cells the spike and notch drawer are at different corners. Requirement cannot be met without violating collision rules.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
